content: When using larger batch percents, fewer models are generated than when using smaller batch percents. This gives any stopping method less points to test whether or not to stop. We also note that kappa agreement scores are generally low between the first few models trained. This, combined with fewer points to stop at, causes BV2009 to stop somewhat sub-optimally when using very large batch percents. Usage of very large batch sizes, such as 10% of the data, is not common so sub-optimal performance of stopping methods in those situations is not a major problem.
